subject: On-prem Order Form / License scope & escrow-like snapshot proposal
messages:
From: Anya Patel <anya.patel@remedyhealth.com>

Cc: procurement@remedyhealth.com, legal+redlines@remedyhealth.com

Subject: Clarify on-prem license footprint + evidence for audit (RemedyHealth)

Hi Soojin,

Thanks again for the demo last week. Procurement and Legal are reviewing the MSA and the Order Form for our planned on-prem deployment. Before we proceed to signing, we need clarity on a few items that have come up in our internal review:

- License scope: We need confirmation that the license covers a single named-cluster deployment (one datacenter) with up to 10 dedicated inference nodes; is horizontal scaling/secondary site explicitly excluded or do we need an addendum?
- Audit evidence: RemedyHealth requires a pathway to validate runtime and snapshot integrity for our internal auditors. SOC2 reports are fine, but we also want a description of your snapshot/escrow-like process (who holds snapshots, what triggers release, and how operator access is witnessed).
- KMS / key custody: Our security team expects that customer-managed KMS will be supported for data at rest keys; what are the integration touchpoints and constraints?

I'm attaching our initial redlines to the MSA and a short procurement checklist. Can you confirm whether Redwood can accept a limited escrow-like deposit (snapshot + verification hash) with a mutually agreed custodian? If not, what alternative evidence flows do you offer?

Target: procurement would like a response and any proposed language by end of week so they can move to PO.

Thanks,
Anya Patel
Senior Procurement Manager
RemedyHealth

--

From: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Clarify on-prem license footprint + evidence for audit (RemedyHealth)

Hi Anya — thanks for the clear list. Below is an initial answer and next steps; copying Legal and Engineering for specific redline proposals and the technical handoff.

Answers (high-level):
- License scope: Standard Order Form covers a single named deployment by default. We can offer an explicit secondary-site addendum (paid) or include language that allows failover testing within the named territory. I'll propose specific Order Form language in the next email.
- Snapshot / escrow-like deposit: Redwood supports a witnessed snapshot process: we can produce an encrypted snapshot + SHA256 digest, and deposit the digest (not the secrets) with a mutually agreed custodian. We can also offer an operator-witnessing window (on-site or remote) for the snapshot verification. This is not the same as full escrow but often satisfies auditor requirements.
- KMS: We support customer-managed KMS integrations (AWS KMS, Google Cloud KMS, Azure Key Vault) for data-at-rest; for on-prem we can integrate with a KMIP-compatible key manager via a secure gateway. There are limits on in-place key rotation during active inference — Engineering will outline constraints.

Action items:
1) Marissa: propose redline text for an "Operator Witnessing & Snapshot" exhibit and an Order Form clause that pins the named deployment and defines secondary-site rights.
2) David: produce short engineer note on how snapshots are produced/verified and KMS integration constraints.
3) Soojin: I will circulate a draft Order Form and timeline to get to PO.

I attached our draft Order Form and a template for the snapshot evidence flow. Expect a redline propose by EOD Wed.

Regards,
Soojin
Director, Sales Engineering
Redwood Inference

Soojin / team — draft redlines attached. Key points I added:

- License language: Firmly pin the Order Form to a "Named Deployment Site" (address + region) and include explicit language that any additional sites require an Order Form amendment. This prevents ambiguous entitlement across failover clusters.
- Snapshot / evidence exhibit: Proposed Exhibit X describes: snapshot generation process, SHA256 digest deposit with a neutral escrow agent, timelines for verification, and a two-party witness procedure. I kept release triggers narrow (bankruptcy, insolvency, or Redwood failure to support the runtime).
- Audit access: Added a limited temporary console access window (read-only, timeboxed) for auditors with MFA + signed NDA and an operator witness present. This is timeboxed to 4 hours per audit instance and requires 30 days notice.
- KMS: Redlined that Redwood will: integrate with customer KMS for encryption-at-rest keys, but private key custody remains with customer; Redwood will not accept custody of master keys.

I deliberately tightened release triggers for the snapshot to reduce commercial risk. If Remedy insists on broader triggers we should discuss commercial compensation.

Please review and flag any business-impactful changes.

Marissa

Marissa / Soojin — thank you for the fast turnaround and thoughtful draft. A few counterpoints from our counsel: 

- Release triggers: Our auditors require the ability to validate software continuity in a limited set of scenarios beyond insolvency (material breach followed by 45 days of cure failure; change of control that materially affects support levels). Please can Redwood consider adding these two triggers?
- Witnessing window: 4 hours per audit is tight for some of our internal processes. Can we expand to an 8-hour window or allow up to two consecutive 4-hour windows per audit instance?
- Operator access: For sensitive workloads we need the ability for RemedyHealth to nominate an independent witness (third party) to observe the operator verification. Is that acceptable?

We're comfortable with the Named Deployment language but will need the Order Form to list exact resource ceilings (nodes, vCPU, GPU type). I'll attach an updated procurement checklist that specifies our expected node counts and a proposed PO schedule.

Hi all — technical note on snapshots, KMS, and witnessing logistics: 

- Snapshot generation: We produce a consistent encrypted VM/container snapshot of the runtime artifact plus a metadata bundle that includes version, model hash, and environment manifest. We sign the metadata bundle and publish a SHA256 digest. The snapshot payload remains encrypted; we can either deposit the encrypted package with a neutral custodian or provide the digest only.
- Witnessing: Remote witnessing (screen-share + session logs) is the lowest-friction option. For on-site, we can support a runbook walk-through with a designated Redwood operator present. If Remedy nominates an independent witness, they must sign our standard witness NDA and follow operator access rules.
- KMS: For KMIP/KMS integrations, we require a gateway that exposes a TLS endpoint accessible from the runtime. Key rotation during an active inference window will require a short restart (~3–7 minutes) for token/agent rekeying; plan for a maintenance window if you expect frequent rotations.

I'll draft a short technical exhibit describing the snapshot digest workflow and the minimal witness checklist for legal. Expect that by EOD.

-David

Anya / Kelly — thanks for the back-and-forth and the visibility into Remedy's audit needs. Quick summary & proposed timeline so procurement can proceed: 

Agreements in principle:
- Order Form will be a Named Deployment exhibit with explicit resource ceilings (we'll insert exact node/GPU counts per Remedy's checklist).
- Snapshot evidence: Redwood will provide an encrypted snapshot + signed metadata bundle and publish the SHA256 digest. Digest will be deposited with a neutral custodian (mutually agreed). Release triggers will include insolvency and material breach; Redwood will consider adding a change-of-control trigger with narrow carveouts. Material-breach trigger requires 45 days cure period (as Remedy requested) — Marissa to propose final language consistent with our risk tolerance.
- Witnessing: We will support remote witnessing by default; Remedy may nominate an independent witness subject to witness NDA and operator-runbook constraints. Witnessing windows can be extended to 8 hours for complex audits; subject to scheduling with Redwood ops.
- KMS: We will accept customer-managed KMS; key custody remains with the customer. David outlined rotation constraints and potential short restart.

Next steps & timeline: 
1) Marissa to circulate final legal redline reflecting the agreed release triggers and witness language — target: Thu EOD 6 Aug.
2) David to publish technical exhibit (snapshot digest flow + witness checklist) — target: Thu EOD 6 Aug.
3) Soojin to circulate updated Order Form with resource ceilings for Remedy to sign — target: Fri noon 7 Aug.

If these targets work, procurement indicated they can issue PO by Friday afternoon. Please flag any blockers.

Best,
Soojin
